# Web API of Wren (Wasm imports)

Every function a page or worker module can import, generated from `api/*.widl`. The same description produces the
host trampolines (`src/page/api_generated.odin`), the Odin guest SDK (`sdk/odin/web`), these pages and the
conformance tests (`examples/apiconformance`, `src/tools/apiconformance`).

## ABI

| IDL type | wasm parameters | host implementation receives | Odin guest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `i32` `u32` `i64` `u64` `f32` `f64` | the same value | the same | the same |
| `bool` | i32 (0 = false) | `bool` | `bool` |
| `string` | address, length (bytes) | `string`, valid UTF-8 (else an error) | `string` |
| `usvstring` | address, length | `string`, invalid sequences replaced by U+FFFD | `string` |
| `bytes` | address, length | `[]u8` | `[]u8` |
| `out bytes` | address, capacity | `[]u8` to fill | `[]u8` |
| `optional string` / `bytes` | address, length = all ones when absent | `Maybe(...)` | `Maybe(...)` |
| `T[]` (numbers, handles) | address, element count | `[]T` (handles: `[]u64`) | `[]T` |
| handle (`Node`, `URL`, ...) | i64 (0 = null) | `Api_<Handle>%!(MISSING ARGUMENT)%!(MISSING CLOSE BRACE)andle, data}` when the API checks it, else `u64` | distinct `u64` |
| `enum` / `flags` | i32 or u32 | `Api_<Enum>` / `bit_set` (out of range = an error) | enum / bit_set |
| `struct` | one wasm value per field, in order | `Api_<Struct>` | struct |
| callback | i32: index in the module's function table | `u32` | procedure value |

Addresses and lengths are i32 for a module whose memory 0 is 32-bit and i64 for a memory64 module: the browser
defines each import with the width of the importing module's memory 0, which is the memory every pointer refers to
(other memories of a multi-memory module are not visible to the browser).

Results:

* a number, bool, enum or handle is the wasm result;
* a `string` (or `bytes`) result takes two more parameters, a buffer (address, capacity) the browser fills with
  what fits; the wasm result (address-sized) is the full length, so a guest can retry with a bigger buffer;
* a function that `raises` returns an i32 status: 0, or a negative `Error`; its result, if any, is written to a
  return pointer (the last parameter; a string result keeps the buffer convention, a negative length being the error);
  the message of the last error is `Exception_message` (module `web`);
* a struct result is always written to a return pointer (C layout, natural alignment).

A pointer outside the memory is a trap (as an out-of-bounds load would be). An argument the browser cannot accept
(invalid UTF-8 in a `string`, a handle that is not live or of another kind, an enum out of range) is an error for a
function that raises (`Type`, `Invalid_Handle`, `Invalid_Argument`) and a trap for one that does not.

Availability: `Window` = page modules, `Worker` = dedicated worker modules; a worker module that imports a
function not exposed to workers is not instantiated.
